plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like blooms. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from single-petaled forms to fully double flowers. It thrives in partially shaded, acidic, well-drained soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Pacific coastal regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant used to make all true tea, and camellia flowers were beloved by Japanese samurai as symbols of nobility.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that blooms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. Its fragrant flowers appear in the cold of late winter, and it is a cherished symbol of perseverance and hope in East Asian culture.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across Japan, Korea, and China, and in botanical gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms often bloom through snow, and in Japan, ume viewing (hanami) traditionally precedes cherry blossom viewing by several weeks.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree or large shrub with sickle-shaped foliage and dense, fluffy golden flower balls. Although it mostly flowers in late winter and spring in Australia, some wattle species bloom in different months across the continent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia (July to October); other Acacia species flower in the Southern Hemisphere summer
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Plumeria rubra
plants.description: A tropical deciduous shrub or small tree with thick, succulent branches and clusters of intensely fragrant, waxy flowers. It flowers heavily in warm weather and in tropical regions can bloom for much of the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere and warm months in the tropics; February is peak bloom in places like Brazil, Fiji, and northern Australia
plants.location: Native to Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean; cultivated throughout the tropics including Hawaii, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific Islands
plants.funFact: Frangipani flowers are pollinated by hawkmoths, yet they produce no nectar and trick the moths into pollinating them through their scent alone.
